commands.author: ralf003

target.title: fix(agents): extract Undici cause.code for ECONNRESET/ECONNREFUSED/ETIMEDOUT
target.body:
## Problem
Undici (Node.js `fetch()` implementation) wraps SocketError (ECONNRESET, ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT) in a cause chain. The current code in `extractTransportErrorDetails` reads `error.code`, `error.error`, and `error.errorCode`, but misses `error.cause.code` where Undici stores these network error codes.

## Fix
Added `error.cause.code` as the final fallback in `extractTransportErrorDetails` before returning the raw error message. One line changed in production code.

## Changes
- `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts`: One-line addition — reads `error.cause.code` as final fallback, and exports `extractTransportErrorDetails` for testability
- `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.test.ts`: 2 new unit tests
  - Undici cause.code extraction test (simulates real Undici error shape)
  - Priority verification (cause.code checked last, never shadows existing paths)

## Testing
- 24/24 tests passing (agents-core + agents-support)

## Real Behavior Proof

### Live Undici Error Capture (2026-07-18, Node.js v24.16.0)

Real `fetch()` call to a closed port via Undici:

```json
{
  "name": "TypeError",
  "message": "fetch failed",
  "cause": {
    "code": "ECONNREFUSED",
    "errno": -4078,
    "syscall": "connect"
  }
}
```

**Key observation**: `top-level error.code` is `undefined` on Undici-fetch failures. The error code (`ECONNREFUSED`) is only available at `error.cause.code`. Without this fix, `extractTransportErrorDetails` returns `errorCode: undefined`, and the failover classifier (`classifyFailoverReasonFromCode`) cannot identify the error as a transient network failure.

### Reproduction Script Output

```
REAL UNDICI fetch() ERROR SHAPE VERIFICATION

Test 1: fetch("https://127.0.0.1:19999") -> TypeError: fetch failed
  Top-level code: undefined
  cause.code: ECONNREFUSED
  Fix effective: YES — cause.code is the only source of the error code

Test 2: fetch("https://127.0.0.1:1443") -> TypeError: fetch failed
  Top-level code: undefined
  cause.code: ECONNREFUSED
  Fix effective: YES — same Undici wrapping behavior
```

### Full Error Code Extraction Test

```
6 Undici network error types tested (ECONNRESET, ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT, ENOTFOUND, UND_ERR_SOCKET, UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT):
  Before fix: All 6 return errorCode=undefined (failover NOT triggered)
  After fix:  All 6 return correct errorCode (failover correctly triggered as "timeout")

3 non-Undici error types tested:
  All unchanged — priority order preserved
```

### Failover Chain

```
fetch() -> ECONNRESET
  -> Undici wraps: TypeError { message: "fetch failed", cause: { code: "ECONNRESET" } }
  -> extractTransportErrorDetails (before fix): errorCode = undefined
  -> classifyFailoverReasonFromCode(undefined) = null (no failover)
  -> REQUEST FAILS

  -> extractTransportErrorDetails (after fix): errorCode = "ECONNRESET"
  -> classifyFailoverReasonFromCode("ECONNRESET") = "timeout"
  -> Failover to next provider
  -> REQUEST SUCCEEDS
```

## Risk
Extremely low. One-line logic change, new code path only activates when existing fallbacks fail, no existing behavior modified. The `cause.code` path is the last resort in the chain (`errorCode` > `code` > `error.code` > `cause.code`).
